# Issue #58 error-swallowing source inventory

This is the authoritative review inventory for the approved
[issue #58 audit](2026-08-13-issue-58-error-swallowing-audit.md). It is review
evidence, not a syntax gate: the spellings below can denote expected control
flow, propagation, or an unexpected failure erased before intentional
continuation.

## Population recipes

The commands were rerun verbatim from the repository root against the final tree
on 2026-08-14. A raw count is the number of output records emitted by the
command before syntax-node exclusions or union deduplication. Five recipe
records contain one additional distinct normalized expression; the reduction
preserves each expression even though the raw command count remains
record-based. Expanding the roots did not change any pre-existing multiline
match.

## Deterministic reduction

1. Preserve each command's output record and recipe membership. The path globs
   remove conventional `tests/`, `benches/`, `fixtures/`, and `examples/`
   directories before the raw count.
2. Resolve the matching source line to its enclosing Rust syntax item. Exclude
   only a line enclosed by the complete `#[cfg(test)]` syntax node, a
   test/bench/example target, a fixture-only `test_support`/`testdata` subtree,
   or rustdoc text/code. Determine `cfg(test)` containment from syntax-node line
   ranges, not byte offsets in comment-scrubbed text; this keeps the production
   item immediately before a test module. Ordinary comments, production doctest
   tooling, and items carrying `cfg_attr(feature = "test-utils", ...)` remain
   included.
3. Name the innermost containing function/method/closure-owning item; use the
   enclosing macro or named item when there is no function. Quote each complete
   matched expression and normalize only whitespace (runs become one ASCII
   space; tokens otherwise remain unchanged). A multiline output record
   containing distinct expressions yields one expression occurrence per
   expression; identical occurrences retain all source lines on one key.
4. Deduplicate on `(path, containing symbol, normalized expression)`. First
   merge repeated occurrences in the same recipe family, then merge
   recipe-family memberships for the same key. Sort rows by path, symbol, then
   expression. Manual high-risk flow conclusions use the same key and appear
   after the recipe union.
5. Classify from the approved target semantics: `expected` is a
   validation/domain/conditional absence stated in the row; `propagated` already
   preserves failure or is assigned to the exact remediation task that must do
   so; `continued` is a deliberately preserved primary result after an
   unexpected failure and therefore records its static context, current report
   site, why continuation is correct, and exact behavioral-proof task.
6. Delivery reconciliation freezes every pre-implementation remediation key in
   the checked ledger below before classified rows move or disappear. The final
   checker validates those obligations without scanning Rust syntax.

899 unique key-family memberships. Twenty-six keys carry a second family
membership, so $899 - 26 = 873$ unique recipe keys. Seventeen source-read
high-risk conclusions remain disjoint from the recipe union, producing 890
authoritative rows.

removed selected expression remains a delivered obligation in the ledger rather
than disappearing from the audit history.
